subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should the bundled Slack plugin own RTS workspace search, and what action-token, scope, read-target, and redaction contract should govern `assistant.search.context` calls?
rationale: The feature crosses ephemeral Slack action tokens, workspace-wide search visibility, and OpenClaw's existing Slack read authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent security contract.

options.title: Add narrow RTS support
options.body: Implement Slack-owned RTS search with ephemeral action-token handling, explicit read-target/security behavior, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external plugin
options.body: Leave bundled Slack unchanged and require a ClawHub/plugin path until maintainers want OpenClaw core to own the search boundary.

options.title: Reject workspace search for now
options.body: Keep Slack on conversation history/thread reads and close future search PRs unless a maintainer sponsors the privacy model.

recommendation.title: Add narrow RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement Slack-owned RTS search with ephemeral action-token handling, explicit read-target/security behavior, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest adjacent Slack action-parity and maintainer-routing history for the unresolved search surface.
